inventory_summary: 123 pipe runs (supply PEX/copper, DWV PVC, vents, radon, sump, condensate) dumped from the resolved model with OD, slopes per segment, insulation; 13 cleanouts; 31 sleeves present; 71 fixture ports (AFF heights); checks mep.drain_slope/vent_grade/trap_arm/riser_through_deck/run_through_stud/plate read. Sheets P-101..P-104 (pages 136-139) and P-201..P-204 (140-143) opened; P-20x are stormwater/roof drainage only (DWV is on P-10x). Baseline UNKNOWNs: riser_through_deck x46 are all I-joist/truss web holes where the fabricator's chart is needed (correct UNKNOWN, 3" drain 3.50" under the 4" bore); run_through_stud/plate UNKNOWNs are a cripple under 2 depths and 3.50" in 2x4 (M2-006). NOT examined: per-sleeve annulus fits (mep_sleeves), hydrant freeze/bury geometry beyond check text, sump/radon vertical riser OD vs deck holes, web-searches of fixture products (I2 seam), copper type L OD vs wall thickness, cleanout code clearance basis.
verified_clean: pipe_sections.py: IPS ODs (PVC DWV 1.5=1.900, 2=2.375, 3=3.500, 4=4.500) and CTS/PEX ODs (1/2=0.625, 3/4=0.875, 1=1.125, 1-1/4=1.375) match ASTM D2665/B88; material routing correct (PEX/copper tube, PVC IPS, None -> IPS).

Drain slope: every horizontal DWV segment >= 0.250 in/ft (flattest PR-B-MAIN-DRAIN seg3 0.250, kitchen/bath drains 0.25-0.30); engine encodes UPC 708.0 1/4"/ft at all sizes (MN is UPC), so the brief's 1/8" >=3" is deliberately not used; 4" main has no reduced-slope approval.
Trap arm table (30/42/60/72/120 in) matches UPC 906.1 as adopted by MN 4714 (distance measurement is M2-003).
Vent runs are monotone rising (mep.vent_grade pass 14); 1/8" margin advisory only.
Cleanouts: 13 resolved, sizes equal pipe size (4" on 4", 3" on 3", 2"/1.5"), 18-24" clearance per drain_cleanouts.py; 100 ft and 135 deg rules coded.
Fixture water/drain heights: WC supply 8-9.5" AFF, lav 24-25.5" AFF/drain 20-21.5", showers valve 48.75" (30.75" tub-shower) are conventional rough-in values.
Hot-water insulation spec strings (1" and 1/2" fiberglass) pass mep.hot_water_insulation; wet_wall_occupancy uses the insulated envelope (2.88").
mep.riser_through_deck UNKNOWN: read body; holes are clear of both I-joist flanges and the 3.50" OD is under the 4" a trade drills; UNKNOWN is the right verdict (fabricator chart).

findings.title: Pipe size labels on P-101..P-104 print nominal with :.0f: 1/2" PEX reads 0", 3/4" reads 1", 1-1/2" reads 2"

evidence.measured: label f'{diameter_in:.0f}"' -> 0.5 prints '0"' (banker's rounding), 0.75 and 1.25 print '1"', 1.5 prints '2"'. Sheet P-103/P-104 show '2" VENT' for the 1-1/2" PR-S-... / PR-A-STUBATH-SH-VENT runs; 113 of 123 runs are not whole-inch.
evidence.expected: 1/2", 3/4", 1-1/4", 1-1/2" printed as fractions (the sizes the plumber orders)
evidence.method: read plumbingplan.py:107-108; python: f'{0.5:.0f}', f'{1.5:.0f}'; pickled model runs diameter_m/0.0254; view P-103 p.138 vent labels

findings.source: ASME/IPS nominal size convention; model diameter_m
findings.proposed_fix: format nominal as a mixed fraction (e.g. 1-1/2")

findings.title: Plumbing-plan slope label is whole-run average (incl. risers), not pipe grade: drains read 4.79"/FT when horizontal grade is 0.29"

evidence.measured: slope=(z_start-z_end)/length_m*... over total developed length including vertical legs: PR-B-KITCH-DRAIN 4.79 in/ft vs per-segment 0.26-0.30; PR-B-MAIN-DRAIN 3.84 vs 0.25; PR-B-WC2-DRAIN 5.16; vents print negative (-0.04..).
evidence.expected: label the horizontal grade the plumber must hold (min 1/4"/ft, UPC 708.0), or omit on runs with risers
evidence.method: .venv/bin/python probe over model.pipe_runs: segment h=plan length, dz=z[i+1]-z[i]; compare with label formula; sheet P-101 p.136

findings.proposed_fix: label per horizontal segment (min of segments with plan run > 1 ft)

findings.title: mep.trap_arm_length grades straight-line plan distance to the nearest vent point, not developed arm length; FX-B-BATH-WC arm is ~10 ft against a 6 ft (72") limit

evidence.measured: Check reports 67" (WC to vent) PASS vs 72". PR-B-BATH-VENT (1.5") is a stub at (120.0,229.5) joining only the utility sink drop; WC drain goes (144,291.8)->(144,208.8) 83"->(120,208.8) 24"->up sink drop 21" = ~128" plan + vertical to the vent tee, 3D gap WC drain to vent run 33". FX-S-BATH1-WC (70" straight, developed 97") and FX-M-BATH1-WC (74" by my nearest-point, drain to vent 3D gap 130") are also near/over the limit.
evidence.expected: trap arm length measured along the drain from the trap weir to the vent connection <= 72" for 3" (UPC 906.1 as coded)
evidence.method: plumbing_dwv.py:436-465 uses hypot(vent_point - drain_point); .venv/bin/python probe: pickle model, walk PR-B-BATH-DRAIN path from FX-B-BATH-WC, scratchpad M2/p5.py p6.py

findings.source: MN Plumbing Code 4714 Table 906.1 (as in takeoff/plumbing_calc.TRAP_ARM_MAX_IN)
findings.proposed_fix: measure developed length along the serving drain to the vent's tee; likely author a real vent tee/riser for the basement WC (or a wet-vent) -- escalate (moves pipe)

findings.title: Vent runs hang in the ceiling plane with no riser or tee to the drain they serve; vent-to-drain 3D gaps 90-130" on 14 fixtures

evidence.measured: e.g. PR-M-WC-VENT z=116"..231" starts at (75,300) vs PR-B-WC1-DRAIN end (72,262) z=-17": 38" in plan and 133" vertical; FX-M-BATH2-SH/TUB/LAUNDRY-SINK vent PR-M-BATH2-VENT 3D gap 115-125"; second-floor fixtures 89-116". Connections exist only by 'serves' lists, so riser lengths, fittings and bores for the missing risers are not modelled/billed.
evidence.expected: each vent connects to its drain by a modelled riser/tee within the trap-arm limit
evidence.method: scratchpad M2/p5.py: sample 3D polylines of each fixture's drain and vent runs and take minimum distance

findings.proposed_fix: author the connecting vent risers (or add a check that the vent run touches the drain run in 3D)

findings.title: Insulated hot-water runs bore studs/plates at bare pipe OD while the sleeve continues through (0.88" graded; 1.88-2.88" real)

evidence.measured: mep.run_through_stud passes PR-B-HW-WASH at 0.88" through W-M-BA2E/W-M-CLN 2x4 non-bearing studs (limit 2.10"); the run wears 1" fiberglass: OD 0.875+2x1 = 2.875" (the wall-cavity check itself uses 2.88" for HW-BATH1). A 2.875" hole exceeds the 60% = 2.10" R602.6 limit in a 2x4 stud and 5/8" edge clearance.
evidence.expected: bore sized to what passes: pipe OD + insulation (or insulation stopped and field note), <= 60% (2.10") in 2x4 non-bearing
evidence.method: checks.json run_through_stud messages for '-HW-' tags; mep_envelopes.py:127 radii use pipe_outside_diameter_m(run.diameter_m, material) with no insulation term; grep 'insulation' in resolve/mep_bores*

findings.source: IRC R602.6; insulation string on PipeRun
findings.proposed_fix: add insulation thickness (parse spec or add field) to the bore OD; or author sleeves stopping short of studs

findings.title: 3" DWV (3.50" OD) stack and arm run in 2x4/4.5" walls and plates: pipe fills the whole stud depth, hubs (~4") cannot fit

evidence.measured: PR-M-S-BATH1-DRAIN (3", vertical at (60.0",319.5") from z=123" to -22") sits on W-M-STOS axis, a 4.5" wall with 2x4 studs and plates (mep.run_through_plate UNKNOWN: 3.50" = plate width, framed opening needed); PR-A-STUBATH-DRAIN 3" through 2x4 stud-005 of W-S-DC2 (mep.run_through_stud UNKNOWN). 3.500 OD vs 3.50 depth leaves zero for fittings (3" DWV hub OD ~4.0-4.2") and 1/2" gypsum is the only cover.
evidence.expected: wet wall deep enough for the 3" fittings (2x6 / furred), plates framed with header
evidence.method: model.walls W-M-STOS thickness 4.5 members {'2x4':9,'2x8':1}; baseline checks.json run_through_plate / run_through_stud UNKNOWN messages; hub OD from Charlotte Pipe 3" sanitary tee dims (library/fittings.py _STACK_DIMS shows 3.0625 stop-to-stop)

findings.source: Charlotte Pipe SUB-PAC-PVC-DWV (cited in library/fittings.py); IRC R602.6/R602.6.1
findings.proposed_fix: furr W-M-STOS locally to 2x6 depth or move the stack to a 2x6 wet wall; escalate (wall thickness, door D-M-BATH1 clearances)

findings.title: Fitting laying lengths are None in the catalog, so no fitting solid or offset is drawn or graded (long-sweep 90, wyes, closet bends)

evidence.measured: every center_to_face_in is None; only Charlotte stack stations (tee/wye/combo/street) carry numbers. evidence.expected: centre-to-face per size from Charlotte submittal (1/4 bend 3" ~4.5", 2" ~3.5")
evidence.method: read library/fittings.py header and _NO_SUBMITTAL; python MEP_FITTINGS center_to_face_in

findings.proposed_fix: read the remaining submittal pages (known debt, Phase 5 routing)
